newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai current account deficit improves further.
newsitem.headline: Thai current account deficit improves further.

text.p: Thailand's monthly current account deficit in July narrowed to 30.8 billion baht from 35.4 billion in June, the central bank said on Thursday.
The deficit in May was 30.7 billion baht (US$1.23 billion) and 48.4 billion in April, showing an overall improving trend over the past three months, it said.

Bank of Thailand (BOT) economist, Suchada Kirakul, told reporters after releasing leading monthly economic indicators, that the trade deficit, however, widened in July while exports remained weak in the month.
Revised bank data showed the July trade deficit at 35.3 billion baht for July, against an earlier estimate of 30 billion baht, and 36.9 billion in June.

Thai money market liquidity was tight in August, partly due to offshore investor speculation against the baht in late July and early August after devaluation rumours, which helped push up domestic short-term interbank rates.
She said tight liquidity was partly eased by an injection of about two billion baht of government reserves in the form of repayments for maturing government bonds.
